summary.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose to INR 18 crore (margin 12.91% vs 0.15%) on revenue of INR 142 crore, while FY26 volume fell 13% to 58,630 MT.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 recovered sharply from a weak prior year: revenue grew 3% YoY to INR 142 crore and EBITDA reached INR 18 crore versus INR 20 lakh a year earlier, with net profit of about INR 4 crore against a loss of INR 4 crore. For the full year, revenue fell 19% to INR 587 crore and volume fell 13%, attributed to heavy rains in operating areas, but EBITDA rose 23% to INR 35 crore and net profit was INR 1 crore versus a loss of INR 4 crore. Management linked Q4 inventory gains to PVC price volatility from the Middle East conflict, and said capex is on hold for two quarters. Several answers deferred to the CFO, reducing detail on freight, dealers and utilisation.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 10,288 MT (+12% YoY); FY26 volume 47,638 MT (-11%). Management cites typical margins of 8-10%, varying by season.

segments.name: Building products
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 2,683 MT (+7% YoY); FY26 volume 7,685 MT (-16%). Margins stated at 14-18%, higher than agriculture; management targets substantial growth in FY27 and CPVC expansion.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 606 MT (-65% YoY); FY26 volume 3,307 MT (-29%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects healthy FY27 volume growth, off a low base, but gave no numeric target; it depends on monsoon conditions.
Management reaffirmed the earlier INR 1,000 crore revenue target and a 10% margin goal by FY28, saying it is 'doing our best'; no ROCE guidance was given.
Building products are to be the main FY27 growth driver, with CPVC expansion; OPVC is not on the agenda.
Capex is on hold; the next decision on capex or a second plant will follow after the first two quarters of FY27.
Inventory gains are possible in Q1 FY27, but management said volatility makes this hard to predict.
capex_capacity: Capex on hold: management says developments are already invested and the next decision comes after the first two quarters of FY27.
No decision on a second manufacturing plant; timing, location and whether to diversify beyond the single central plant are open.
CPVC capacity is being expanded; OPVC capacity is not planned at present.
Q4 plant utilisation described as 'fairly good' and above the company average; no percentage given.
Company runs a single central plant and relies on depots to serve other regions; management said building products can bear distant logistics but agriculture is limited to a regional territory.
demand_pricing: Demand for agri and building products was hit when the Middle East war pushed raw material and finished goods prices up sharply; management says demand is now back to near normal.
Management says PVC prices are volatile after the Iran-Iraq conflict; Q4 included inventory gains, and the company stocked up in March ahead of the April-June agri season.
The government withdrew import duty on PVC and other polymers until about 1 July; management said there is no anti-dumping duty.
Competition is aggressive with many national players present in MP; branded players are gaining share from unorganised ones.
Market share: MP and Rajasthan described as strong, Maharashtra sub-10% and still in development; dealer count about 400, with expansion mainly in adjacent regions.
PVC resin is sourced from a mix of imports and local purchases; management gave no split.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be inventory gains in Q1 FY27, and when will volume growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 may still show some inventory advantage but this is hard to predict given volatility. Demand has normalised after the war, and FY27 growth is expected from a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex being put on hold, and how will the company compete outside its central plant location?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is on hold until the first two quarters of FY27 are reviewed. Management said expansion beyond the region is limited for agri but feasible for building materials, and any new capacity will be carefully considered.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 show negative gross margin before inventory adjustments, and was the stocking strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March inventory build is routine, to prepare for the April-June agri season, and gave no figures.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall 33% in FY26, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said other expenses mainly comprise freight; the CFO would provide the breakdown offline. No figures were given on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Has the building products segment crossed INR 100 crore, and what is the expected contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said building products revenue fell in FY26 due to rationalisation and will see a quantum jump in FY27, but gave no figure for the segment's FY26 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables fall, from INR 48 crore to INR 28 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivables are mostly from institutional customers, which the company cut in Q4 as planned.

risks_watch: Volatile PVC prices: inventory gains helped Q4 and could reverse, and the policy on import duty expires around 1 July.

Q4 cost of materials consumed (about INR 170 crore per an analyst's read) exceeded revenue of INR 142 crore, so the margin is inventory-driven; the sustainability of the 12.91% Q4 EBITDA margin is unproven.
FY26 volume declined 13%; FY27 recovery depends on monsoon conditions and needs to be seen in Q1-Q2 results.
Single-plant concentration limits reach outside central India, and aggressive competition from national players may pressure pricing.
Capex and second-plant decision deferred to after H1 FY27; ROCE of about 7% for FY26 remains low versus the FY28 targets.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term outlook: management stresses volatility and uncertainty on PVC prices and monsoon, while expressing confidence in FY27 recovery from a low base. Evasive on several specifics (dealer split, utilisation numbers, freight breakdown, FY28 ROCE), deferring to the CFO offline.
